objects.name: a folded stack of evening papers

people.name: Antonio Marchetti
people.role: a photographer for the rotogravure section

secret.description: Antonio Marchetti is alone with Maureen Quill in the Roof Garden from 8:30 PM to 9:00 PM, and kills Maureen Quill at 9:00 PM.
Willa Prentiss hands a parcel of stolen goods to a man at the Kitchen at 9:00 PM.
Delia Mulcahy slips out to the Street from 8:30 PM to 9:00 PM to settle with a bookmaker.

people.name: Marion Winslow
people.role: a wine steward out of work since the Act

secret.description: Marion Winslow is not the person the register says. Nothing is hidden about the evening; the lie is in the paperwork.

people.name: Lorraine Ashby
people.role: a stringer for the evening papers

secret.description: Lorraine Ashby goes through the papers in the Victim's Suite from 7:00 PM to 7:30 PM while the victim is downstairs.

people.name: Beatrice Ellery
people.relationshipToVictim: a childhood friend of the victim from the same block

secret.description: Beatrice Ellery drinks alone in the Bar from 8:30 PM to 9:00 PM and will claim to have been anywhere else.

method.name: strangling with a cord
method.bodyEvidence: A ligature furrow across the throat. Three fibres of hemp in the skin.

Maureen Quill was found in the Roof Garden. The coroner puts death between 8:30 PM and 9:00 PM. A ligature furrow across the throat. Three fibres of hemp in the skin.
A length of sash cord is missing from the Kitchen. A cut end of the same hemp is still tied to the fitting it was taken from.
Rain began at 9:30 PM and did not let up. Anyone out on the street after that came back in wet.
Antonio Marchetti says Delia Mulcahy came in off the street at 11:30 PM with a soaked coat, so Delia Mulcahy was outside at 11:00 PM.
Marion Winslow's papers do not hold up. A steamship ticket stub in the name of a man who died at Belleau Wood.
Found in the Victim's Suite: A subpoena naming Maureen Quill as a witness before the grand jury, with Antonio Marchetti's name written in the margin.
Martin Feeney says Maureen Quill said to Antonio Marchetti that a man who testifies sleeps better.
Found in the Front Desk: A promissory note for $4,000 signed by Willa Prentiss, endorsed to Maureen Quill, three months past due.
Martin Feeney says Maureen Quill told Willa Prentiss that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
Found in the Front Desk: Three letters in Maureen Quill's hand to a woman Lorraine Ashby is engaged to, kept in the drawer, the last one opened.
Willa Prentiss says Lorraine Ashby told Maureen Quill to keep away, loud enough to turn heads.
